intro_html: Feijoada is the national dish of Brazil, and it started the way most great dishes start, with cooks making something extraordinary out of the cuts nobody else wanted. Black beans and several kinds of pork go into one pot and cook until the beans break down into a dark, glossy gravy. Served over white rice on a Saturday, it is the meal an entire country slows down for.
cost_closing_html: About $3.99 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a dish with four different meats in it. Black beans are the cheapest protein in the store and they are what let this pot carry that much pork without wrecking the math.
shop_smart: Beans are the point, not the filler. Black beans give this dish its body, its color and a good chunk of its protein, and they cost less per serving than almost anything else you can put in a pot.
Buy the pork shoulder, use the trimmings. Feijoada was built on scraps. Every bit of fat and every bone you throw in makes the gravy richer, so buy bone-in when you can.
Bacon and diced ham are seasoning meats. Small amounts of each add smoke and salt through the whole pot. This is where a half pound does the job of two.
Slow cooker on low is the right setting. Eight or nine hours is what turns beans into gravy. Rushing it on high gives you beans in broth, which is not the same dish.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the chopped bacon in a skillet, then use that fat to sear the cubed pork shoulder and the cubed beef chuck roast on all sides. Do it in batches so the meat browns instead of steams.
Cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same skillet until soft, scraping up everything stuck to the bottom.

Move the bacon, seared meats, onion and garlic to the slow cooker along with the diced ham, the drained black beans, the chicken broth, the white vinegar, the bay leaves, ground coriander, salt and black pepper.
Cook on low for 8 to 9 hours, until the pork shreds under a fork and the beans have gone soft enough to thicken the liquid.
Mash a scoop of the beans against the side of the crock and stir it back in. That is what turns the broth into gravy.
Pull out the bay leaves, shred the larger pieces of meat, and cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice across your 14 containers, then set your mixing pot on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight of beans and meat over the rice. Every bowl lands near 695 calories with 48 grams of protein, and it is even better on day two.
upsell_html: Brazil's national dish for about $3.99 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Black beans slow cooked with pork shoulder, beef chuck, bacon and ham into a dark gravy over rice. A 14 serving Brazilian feijoada for meal prep.
head.keywords: brazilian feijoada, black bean pork stew, slow cooker feijoada, pork and beans recipe, budget meal prep, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Brown the bacon, then sear the cubed pork shoulder and beef chuck in the fat.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan, scraping up the browned bits.
Combine everything in the slow cooker with the diced ham, black beans, broth, vinegar and bay leaves.
Cook on low 8 to 9 hours until the meat shreds and the beans soften.
Mash some beans to thicken, shred the meat, and serve over cooked rice.
